reason: The passage depicts the moment God commissions Moses to lead the Israelites out of Egypt. God explicitly states 'וְהוֹצֵא אֶת־ עַמִּי בְנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמִּצְרָיִם' (bring forth my people, the children of Israel, out of Egypt). While Moses is not yet an active national leader at this point—he is still a shepherd—the text portrays him as divinely appointed and commissioned to become one. He is positioned as an aspiring national leader through God's explicit call and authorization. His initial protest ('Who am I?') further emphasizes his reluctance but does not negate the text's portrayal of him as called to national leadership.
